To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Untangle is the first recommendation system that gives users control on the recommendations based on specific item attributes (e.g. less violent, funnier).

Untangle: (i) is the first recommendation model that enables users to critique their recommendations with respect to specific attributes; (ii) uses a refined training process which allows it to disentangle item attributes from the latent representation; (iii) is able to generate recommendations that are accurate and relevant to the user's preferences.

Untangle: (1) learns to disentangle the representations of items in a partially supervised manner, (2) is able to generate accurate recommendations, (3) is able to provide recommendations based on specific user preferences.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) how to create disentanged item representations, (ii) how to create a recommendation model that can be critiqued on item attributes, (iii) how to train a recommendation model to be critiqued, (iv) how to create an efficient training procedure to learn item representations and (v) how to evaluate a model that is critiqued.
the following questions: 1. Can we create a recommender system where users have control over the recommendations based on particular item attributes?

the following questions: (i) How can we disentangle the item representations to enable critiquing recommendations? (ii) How can we learn a model that generates accurate recommendations based on the disentangled item representations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paper presents a novel approach to disentangling the latent factors of items and users in recommender systems, and provides a framework to control the recommendations by critiquing the attributes.
Untangle is an effective recommendation model that allows users to control recommendations based on specific item attributes.
the paper proposes a novel approach to recommendation system that allows the user to control the recommendations with respect to specific attributes of an item.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a model that allows users to control their recommendation lists based on specific item aspects, and that can be trained on very little supervision.
we are able to generate recommendations for a user based on the critiquing that user provides.
we propose a novel framework for critiquing based on user preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn disentangled representations of item attributes, that can be used to create critiquable recommender system, with a very small amount of labeled data.
it is possible to train a model to disentangle item representations without the use of any labeled data.
disentangling the latent space can be used to control the recommendations in a principled way.
